goal: Ship a consumer language-learning app people reach for in spare minutes

items.goal: Office workers learning a second language in the gaps of a commuting day
business_rules: A learner may use the app without ever creating a paid account
acceptance: A first-time learner can finish something useful before signing up

items.goal: Learning in fragmented time: on a platform, in a queue, waiting for a meeting
business_rules: Any session must be resumable after an interruption
acceptance: The home screen offers a 2-minute, a 5-minute and a 10-minute session length
Each session length lists the question types it will draw from

items.goal: Learners forget what they studied because review never meets them where the gap is
business_rules: A review that is due today is never silently dropped
acceptance: Due review items appear in the next session the learner starts

items.goal: Spare minutes add up to measurable retention the learner can see
business_rules: Progress is stated in learner terms, never in internal scores
acceptance: After a week a learner can see what they retained and what slipped

items.goal: Free daily practice, paid unlimited review history and offline packs
business_rules: A paywall never interrupts a session already in progress
acceptance: An expired subscription keeps read access to past progress

items.goal: Depth of one language over breadth of many at launch
business_rules: No second language ships before the first one retains learners
acceptance: The launch build offers exactly one language pair

actions.reason: These are the people we are building for
Fragmented time is the situation we serve
Forgetting is the problem worth solving
Free practice, paid history is the model
One language done well comes first

reason: Freeze the launch scope and start planning

exclude.gap-experience-direction: The session never raised the topic; the session-length list was taken as the experience
